The day at a glance

The wine day. Santa Maria around mile 18 sits in one of the state's biggest strawberry and broccoli districts, then Foxen Canyon is the spine of the Santa Maria Valley AVA — a cool, wind-exposed valley that opens west to the ocean, which is why pinot noir and chardonnay do well this far south. The last stretch into Los Olivos and Solvang crosses into the Santa Ynez Valley AVA.

Worth looking up for

  • The best day for small towns: Arroyo Grande Village, Nipomo, Sisquoc, Los Olivos and Ballard are all on or near the route.
  • Rides the length of Foxen Canyon through the Santa Maria Valley wine country — tasting rooms are the main thing open along the middle of the day.

What to watch for

  • No mapped tree cover anywhere on the route.
  • The longest stretch without anywhere to stop is 17 mi, from Santa Maria to the Riverbench winery. Between there and Los Olivos the stops are tasting rooms, whose hours are far less dependable than a shop.
  • Late climb at mi 43.5–44.4, 301 ft at 6.6%, when the day is nearly done.

Stops along the way

Mapped in OpenStreetMap and carried in the GPX as waypoints, so they show on a head unit too. Distances are miles from the start. Tap a name for Google Maps, or the arrow for Apple Maps. Not verified on the ground — opening hours and whether a tap actually runs are anyone’s guess. A star marks a stop somebody picked by hand and vouched for, rather than one the OpenStreetMap query happened to return. Everything else here is within a quarter mile of the line; the few that are further say how far.
